$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs the same steps locally.
`status` is `oracle-backed` (CI regenerates the golden in the pinned container and compares
it on every run) or `unchecked` (the golden is committed and read by the Rust tests, but no
CI step has ever re-derived it). The distinction is part of the claim each suite supports.
Jobs that are analysis rather than comparison stay hand-written in ci.template.yml: the
jmath corpus diff and the pow probe of decision 0007, and the JVM number-format sweep of
decision 0017, which asserts measured rates rather than byte equality.

ci.$why: Suites are grouped into jobs of this size: one job per suite would restore the oracle image once per suite, and one job for all of them is what the hand-written workflow did, where a failing suite hid every suite after it.

suites.title: BGZF blocks
suites.why: The committed goldens were produced under Rosetta on Apple Silicon. If real silicon disagrees, every claim resting on them is void, so this must fail loudly.

compare.why: The corpus is a literal array in the Rust test rather than a .txt.gz, so both sides are read with the same pattern; only the shared cases are compared, since the test carries cases the dump does not emit.

suites.title: BAM record codec
suites.why: The BAM record codec is pure integer work, so unlike the math corpus there is no reason to expect emulation to change it. That is the hypothesis; this measures it, because "no reason to expect" is how decision 0004's wrong assumption got in.

suites.title: BAM file and header
suites.why: These carry compressed bytes, so unlike the record codec they do depend on the deflate implementation. Decision 0001 pins it; this is what would catch that pin coming loose.

suites.title: BAM reheader
suites.why: The reheadered BAM is block-copied, so it carries compressed bytes and depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001), exactly like the BAM file goldens. Comment rows share a (kind, case) key so only the last per case is diffed here, but the reheadered hex encodes every comment in its header, so any comment drift shows up there.

suites.title: BAM gather
suites.why: The gathered BAM is block-copied, so it carries compressed bytes and depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001). Input rows share a (kind, case) key so only the last per case is diffed here, but the gathered hex is the concatenation of them all.

suites.title: BuildBamIndex (read-side BAI)
suites.why: The read-side .bai carries compressed-stream virtual offsets, so it depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001) exactly like the BAM goldens, and it differs from the write-side BAI.

suites.title: Interval lists
suites.why: Some cases have an empty value: an empty interval list is a result, not a missing row, so valueless lines are kept rather than skipped.

suites.title: Reading a VCF header
suites.why: Everything else here writes VCF; nothing reads one, and GATK's VariantWalker cannot exist without a reader. Two layers are measured. VCFHeaderLineTranslator's VCF4Parser is a hand-written scanner whose switch falls through from the '<' case into the '>' case, so an unquoted '<' away from position 0 is dropped, an unquoted '>' anywhere is dropped, and a line that does not end in '>' loses its last field entirely and silently: a port written from the VCF specification would keep those characters and store that field. Quotes are a toggle rather than a delimiter, because the quote test precedes the in-quote test, so a quote in the middle of an unquoted value opens a quoted region and the comma after it stops separating fields; inside a quote a backslash before anything but a quote or a backslash is kept together with the character. VCFCodec.readActualHeader is the second layer: it splits the version line on every '=' and records a version only when that yields exactly two fields, so a line with an extra '=' records nothing and fails later with a different message. The refusals carry their messages because the messages separate two failures of the same file. Only unstructured meta lines are fed to the frame; turning an INFO line into a typed compound header line is the next layer and is measured on its own, since mixing them would leave a failure ambiguous between the two.

suites.title: One ## line into a typed header line
suites.why: The scanner suite says which pairs a line carries; this says what they mean, and it is where the refusals are. Four different exception classes come out of this layer and which one a file gets is a property of the field that is wrong: Number=x throws java.lang.NumberFormatException because nothing wraps Integer.parseInt, Number=-1 throws TribbleException$InvalidHeader, Number=0 on a non-Flag type throws java.lang.IllegalArgumentException from validate(), and Type=integer throws a plain TribbleException without the malformed-header prefix. Two of those are unchecked Java exceptions that no catch in the codec touches, so a malformed Number does not report a malformed header at all, and a port that funnelled every failure into one error type would answer a different question. Three asymmetries make the same line valid or invalid depending on context rather than on the line: INFO allows Type=Flag and FORMAT does not; a Flag with a non-zero count is silently rewritten to zero rather than refused, which is a value change and not an error; and Source and Version are read only from VCF 4.2, while under 4.1 they are not recommended tags either, so the tag-order check rejects the same line the 4.2 codec accepts. The rendered line is compared rather than the fields, because the rendering is what a writer emits and it carries the quoting rule as well as the values.

suites.title: FormatUtil number formatting
suites.why: 41,678 formatted doubles, and the corpus the README's 99.73% rests on. Its harness exists and its Rust test reads it, but no CI step has ever regenerated it against the oracle, so the rate is a property of the machine that produced the file rather than of the pinned reference. Decision 0011 makes this corpus locale-dependent, which is exactly the kind of thing the container pins and a developer machine does not.

probes.title: Decision 0019: is re-sorting a sorted VCF header still a no-op?
probes.on_failure: Re-sorting is no longer stable. Decision 0019 needs revisiting.
probes.why: The port relies on it: writing a header that has already been through the comparator once must not reorder it. Measured stable, not proven stable, so it is re-measured.

probes.title: Decision 0016: is the VCF header comparator still inconsistent?
probes.on_failure: The comparator is now consistent. Decision 0016 can be revisited.
probes.why: The cycle is the reason the port uses a total order where htsjdk has none. If a future htsjdk made the comparator consistent, this fails and the divergence can be removed.

goldens_handled_elsewhere.why: Compared function by function against a corpus regenerated on real silicon, with per-function pass conditions from decision 0007, rather than by byte equality.
